label: Brent Crude
value: $104.33/bbl Sep 18 (+$0.35), after tumbling ~4% to $103.98 Sep 17 on Saudi's partial-restart signal, down from the $108.75 Sep 15 crisis-high
delta: Fell sharply Sep 17 as Saudi Arabia indicated it could restore about half of the East-West pipeline's lost capacity within days; ticked back up Sep 18 after Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fresh cross-border attacks, a new front beyond the pipeline and Yanbu disruptions

label: Saudi East-West Pipeline
value: Shut since Sep 11; Yanbu Red Sea loadings also suspended Sep 15 (~4-5M bpd, 4-5% of global supply); Saudi signals ~half capacity restorable within days, full repair up to 6 weeks
source: The Times of Israel / Business Recorder / CNBC / Kpler (Sep 15-17, 2026)
contestNote: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the outage will be 'measured in days'; UK officials and some industry sources cite repair estimates of five to six weeks; Kpler expects only a partial bypass restoring about half of exports within a month
delta: Aramco suspended crude loadings at Yanbu and cancelled some September cargoes to European customers; total Saudi crude loadings have fallen over 70% (7.5M bpd Jan-Feb to 2.1-2.3M bpd mid-Sep) as exports reroute via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers, the Suez/Sumed pipeline and the Cape of Good Hope

label: Saudi Crude Loadings vs. Pre-Crisis
delta: Replacement flow moving via Sohar ship-to-ship transfers and the Strait of Hormuz itself (2M+ bpd), a smaller volume via Suez/Sumed, and limited use of the much longer Cape of Good Hope route

label: Bab el-Mandeb Daily Transits
delta: New second chokepoint risk: Houthi capture of Yemen's Mokha port and advance toward the strait cut Red Sea vessel crossings from 30 (Wed) to 12 (Thu), narrowing the Suez/Red Sea bypass route shippers have used to avoid the closed Strait of Hormuz

label: US Diesel Price
delta: Crossed $6/gallon for the first time as the Sep 9-10 shipping-attack wave and the new Red Sea front pushed Brent toward its $108 crisis peak

label: FAO Food Price Index
source: FAO (Aug 2026, released Sep 4 -- highest since late 2022)
delta: Up 1.9% from July's revised level and 2.5% y/y; broad-based across all five commodity groups -- sugar +11.9% m/m, cereals +2.2% m/m (highest since May 2024), dairy +2.3% m/m

label: Hormuz Daily Tanker Transits
value: 3 vessels Sep 17 (record low) vs ~10M bbl/day claimed (US)
source: Tanker-tracking data via Al Arabiya / Straits Daily Brief (Sep 17, 2026)
contestNote: President Trump said the US maintains "total control" of the strait and Energy Secretary Chris Wright said roughly 10 million barrels/day -- "two-thirds or north of two-thirds" of pre-war flow -- were moving under the US-led escort regime; independent tanker trackers counted just three vessel transits on Sep 17, the lowest of the crisis, against a 10-day average of roughly 17 and a pre-war daily average of over 100 ships
delta: vs 14 over the Sep 12-13 weekend and 130-140/day (100+ ships) pre-war
deltaNote: Traffic fell further to a fresh record low even as the US insists flows are largely restored; only an empty dry-bulk carrier and a 'dark' tanker with disabled AIS crossed on Sep 17

label: War-Risk Insurance (Hull Value)
value: 7.5-10% (a $100M tanker now faces $3-10M in war-risk premiums)
source: Lloyd's List / Discovery Alert / Aju Press (Sep 15, 2026)
delta: vs 0.125-0.25% pre-crisis; container surcharges now running $1,800-3,800 per box plus an extra $1,000/container for Hormuz transits

label: 2026 Global Growth Forecast
contestNote: World Bank warns growth could fall to 1.3% in an adverse energy-shock scenario; IMF's own baseline is more optimistic at 3.1%

label: People at Risk of Acute Hunger (Conflict-Linked)
contestNote: Figure specific to Middle East conflict spillover; WFP's broader 2026 crisis-hunger caseload (318 million) is separate and driven by multiple conflicts

deltaNote: Concentrated in Saudi Arabia & UAE, both Hormuz-dependent
